title: Commercial management approach, team structure and role descriptions
blurb: Explain the three organization management products in an agile project and decide where a piece of information belongs.
question: A project needs to record how its office-based and remote team members will work together, using tools that keep work visible. Which management product should hold this?

teach.body: The organization practice uses three management products. The commercial management approach sets out how goods and services will be procured and contracted. The project management team structure shows who is involved, how they relate and how they will work together. Role descriptions set out each role in the project management team and its specific responsibilities. PRINCE2 Agile keeps all three and tailors them for agile working.

head: Management product
Purpose in agile
Key contents
rows: Procurement and contracts that support agile
Who, relationships, how they work together
E.g. PM is mentored by the agile coach
teach.caption: Paraphrased from Table 7.3.

teach.body: In agile, the form of procurement and contract must support agile product development. Examples include fixed delivery teams or fixed costs per iteration, a definition of the minimum viable product and its tolerances, an agreed Definition of Done, and guidelines for team self-management and for tracking and reporting. Its contents cover the delivery model, resources for market engagement, procurement and contract management, responsibilities, tools and techniques, standards and references.

The team structure defines who is involved, their relationships and how they will work together. Its working practices should reflect agile ways of working, naming the techniques, metrics and artifacts used across the project, and should include arrangements for co-located or remote teams, with agile techniques and tools that make work transparent and support rich communication. Contents: a structure chart, a summary of authority and responsibilities, working practices and arrangements, and supporting information.

Role descriptions set out the roles of those in the project management team and their specific responsibilities, using the 11 PRINCE2 Agile roles tailored to the project. A typical agile entry is that the project manager will be mentored by the agile coach. The project executive approves the project brief, the management approaches and the project management team structure.

head: Information
Where it belongs

Weekly co-location day, shared online board
PM to be mentored by the agile coach

teach.body: Tidewell Council is hiring an agency to build a parking permit service. Project manager Ruth Okonjo writes into the commercial management approach that the agency supplies a fixed team at a fixed cost per iteration, with an agreed MVP and Definition of Done. The team structure records two co-location days a week and a shared visual board. The role descriptions note that Ruth will be mentored by the agile coach.

teach.text: Co-location and remote-working arrangements belong in the PROJECT MANAGEMENT TEAM STRUCTURE, not in the commercial approach or role descriptions. The commercial approach covers how suppliers are procured and contracted, not the supplier's own agile ways of working.

items: Commercial management approach: procurement and contracts that support agile.
Agile contract features: fixed teams or cost per iteration, MVP and tolerances, agreed DoD.
Team structure: who, relationships, how they work together, agile working practices.
Team structure includes co-location or remote arrangements and transparency tools.
Role descriptions: each role's specific responsibilities (e.g. PM mentored by the agile coach).
The project executive approves the management approaches and the team structure.

summary: You can now explain the purpose of the commercial management approach, the project management team structure and role descriptions in agile. You can also place a piece of information in the right one.

A.q: What is the purpose of the commercial management approach in an agile project?
options: To make sure procurement and contracts support agile development
To show who is involved and how the team will work together
To describe each role's specific responsibilities
To set out how issues and changes will be controlled
A.why: The form of procurement and contract needs to support agile approaches to product development (Table 7.3).

whyNot.1: Who is involved and how they work together is the project management team structure.
whyNot.2: Each role's responsibilities are set out in role descriptions.
whyNot.3: Controlling issues and changes is the issue management approach.

A.q: Which is listed as content of the project management team structure?
options: A summary of authority and responsibilities
The project vision and business options
A.why: The team structure contains a structure chart, a summary of authority and responsibilities, working practices and arrangements, and supporting information (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: The delivery model is content of the commercial management approach.
whyNot.2: Benefits measurement and tolerance guidance belongs to the benefits management approach.
whyNot.3: Vision and business options are parts of the project canvas.

A.q: Which feature is an example of a commercial arrangement that supports agile?
options: A fully detailed specification signed off at the start
A penalty for any change to requirements
Fixed delivery teams or costs per iteration
Payment held until the whole product is delivered
A.why: Fixed delivery teams or costs per iteration are given as examples of contracts that support agile development (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: A fixed detailed specification up front works against flexing what is delivered.
whyNot.1: Penalizing change works against agile, which embraces change.
whyNot.3: Agile delivers incrementally; holding all payment to the end does not reflect that.

B.q: Where should arrangements for co-located and remote team members, with tools for transparency, be recorded?
B.why: The team structure's working practices include arrangements for co-located or remote teams, with agile techniques and tools for transparency and rich communication (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: The commercial approach covers procurement and contracts, not team working arrangements.
whyNot.1: Role descriptions set out each role's responsibilities, not working arrangements.
whyNot.2: The communication approach covers means and frequency of communication with stakeholders, not team set-up.

B.q: A project wants to record that its project manager will be mentored by the agile coach. Where does this belong?
B.why: Role descriptions set out each role's specific responsibilities, for example that the PM is mentored by the agile coach (Table 7.3).

whyNot.1: The team structure shows relationships and working practices rather than a role's specific duties.
whyNot.2: The commercial approach covers procurement and contracts.
whyNot.3: The quality approach covers quality techniques, standards and responsibilities for quality.

B.q:
Which two items would appear in an agile-friendly commercial management approach?
1. An agreed Definition of Done.
2. A summary of each team member's skills.
3. A definition of the MVP and its tolerances.
4. A structure chart of the project team.
B.why: An agreed DoD (1) and a definition of the MVP with tolerances (3) are examples of contract features that support agile (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: skills are mapped in the team skill matrix.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: skills go in the skill matrix, and the structure chart is in the team structure.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: the structure chart belongs to the project management team structure.

C.q: Which role approves the project management team structure, and which practice does that product belong to?
C.why: The project executive approves the project management team structure (Table B.1), which is an organization practice product (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: The PM prepares it but does not approve it, and it is not a plans product.
whyNot.1: The CPO represents users; the team structure is not a business case product.
whyNot.3: The practice is right, but the agile coach advises rather than approving.

C.q: A supplier's way of running its own iterations is being discussed. Why is this NOT content of the commercial management approach?
options: It belongs to the risk register as a supplier risk
The approach covers selecting and contracting suppliers
The approach is written by the supplier, not the customer
It is decided by the agile coach in the kickoff workshop
C.why: The commercial approach describes how suppliers are procured and contracted (delivery model, resources, responsibilities), not the supplier's own agile ways of working (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: Supplier working methods are not a risk entry by default; the point is what the approach covers.
whyNot.2: Authorship is not the reason; the approach is about procurement and contracts.
whyNot.3: The agile coach does not decide a supplier's methods, and the kickoff covers team values and matrices.

C.q: Performance reviews and access to project systems are being agreed for a new team. Where should they be recorded, and why?
options: Role descriptions, as they define each role
Commercial approach, as they affect the supplier
Team structure, as part of working practices
Team dashboard, as they show team progress
C.why: The team structure holds working practices and arrangements, which include performance reviews and access to tools and systems (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: Role descriptions list responsibilities, and system access is not a responsibility.
whyNot.1: The commercial approach covers procurement and contracts, not team arrangements.
whyNot.3: The team dashboard shows progress, not working arrangements.

reteach.title: Hiring a band for a festival
reteach.question: If you booked a band for a festival, which document covers the deal, which covers how the crew works together, and which covers each person's job?

blocks.body: The booking contract, with its fee per set and what counts as a finished performance, is the commercial management approach. The crew plan, showing who reports to whom, rehearsal days and the shared running order board, is the project management team structure. The job card for each person, such as 'stage manager is mentored by the festival director', is a role description.

blocks.text: Rehearsal days and the shared board are about how people work together: team structure, not the contract.

explain.body: Procurement and contracts must support agile: fixed teams or cost per iteration, MVP and tolerances, agreed DoD, self-management and reporting guidelines.

items: Resources for market engagement, procurement and contract management

test.q: Which is content of the commercial management approach?
test.why: The commercial approach includes the delivery model, resources, responsibilities, tools and techniques, standards and references (Table 7.3).

whyNot.1: A structure chart is in the project management team structure.
whyNot.2: The release map is the plans practice's project and stage plan.
whyNot.3: The skill matrix is an organization technique, not commercial content.

explain.body: Who is involved, their relationships and how they work together, with agile working practices and co-location or remote arrangements.

items: Tools for transparency and rich communication

test.q: What should the working practices in the team structure reflect?
test.why: The working practices described should reflect agile ways of working and the techniques, metrics and artifacts used across the project (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: Pricing belongs to the commercial management approach.
whyNot.1: Benefits reviews belong to the benefits management approach.
whyNot.3: Risk appetite is the business's attitude to risk, which shapes risk tolerances, not team working practices.

explain.body: The roles of those in the project management team and their specific responsibilities, for example that the PM is mentored by the agile coach.

options: The team's current and future skills
test.why: Role descriptions describe the roles in the project management team and their specific responsibilities (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: Procurement is the commercial management approach.
whyNot.1: Current and future skills are shown in the team skill matrix.
whyNot.2: Remote collaboration arrangements are in the team structure.

explain.body: Contract or supplier deal: commercial approach. How people work together, tools, remote set-up: team structure. One role's duties: role descriptions.

test.q: A team agrees a shared online board and two office days a week. Which product records this?
test.why: Co-location or remote arrangements and transparency tools belong in the team structure's working practices (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: Role descriptions cover one role's responsibilities.
whyNot.1: The commercial approach covers procurement and contracts.
whyNot.2: The communication approach covers stakeholder communication, not team working arrangements.
